# 0010: Per-pod, in-memory rate limit

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-19
- **Modules:** upload-service
- **Source:** design doc, section "Where the rate limit is counted" (linked from README.md in this folder)

## Decision

Count uploads per MAC in each pod's memory, default 30 per 10 minutes, behind a `RateLimiter` interface. A shared
implementation can replace it later without touching callers.

## Rules for agents

Callers use the `RateLimiter` interface only; don't add a network call (Redis, Valkey) to the upload path without a new record.

One full day of pccfg access logs in OCI Log Analytics (`VO_Phone_SSL_log`, us-phoenix-1, Thursday 2026-10-15, UTC).
Read-only queries on 2026-10-16, with MACs and file names masked. One weekday in one region. OCI keeps 5 to 7 days,
so these numbers cannot be re-measured; they are kept here because several decisions rest on them.

| Finding | Result | What it changed |
|---|---|---|
| Daily volume | 11.67 M PUTs and 2.38 M HEADs a day (HEAD only before app.log). By type: calls.xml 65%, app.log 21%, core dumps 13%, then phone.cfg 57 k and boot.log 30 k. | Confirms about 11 M a day. calls.xml is most of the load, so storing or rejecting it is a real decision (ADR 0008). |
| Peak rate | 135/s daily average. Peak hour 15:00 to 16:00 UTC at 272/s; busiest second 532/s. Quietest hour about 46/s. | About twice the brief's 127/s. Replicas and load tests sized for at least 550/s (`docs/load-tests/`). |
| Phones and per-MAC rate | About 600 k phones a day upload app.log and 359 k upload calls.xml. PUTs per MAC in 10 minutes: median 1, p99 6, max 114. One MAC went over 30. | A limit of 30 per 10 minutes is safe for normal phones and catches the outlier (ADR 0010). |
| Retries today, after 405 | app.log repeats about every 64 s; calls.xml at 60, 120 or 300 s; core dumps in quick bursts. 66 k distinct core files were sent 1.52 M times (about 23 each), some dated 2018. | Expect a burst of about 66 k old core dumps once the service answers 200, then normal volume. In the load-test profile. |
| Status codes today | 99.98% of PUTs get 405. Also 408 (about 2.6 k a day), 400 (721), 413 (187, mostly core dumps) and 500 (15). | Some core dumps are very large, possibly over 1 GiB (unverified), which drives the size limits and the timeout headroom (ADR 0005). |
| File names seen | `<MAC>-app.log`, `calls.xml`, `boot.log`, `audit.log`, `plcmsyslog.tar.gz`, `phone.cfg`, `web.cfg`; core dumps in three layouts (`enc.` and `enc1.`); crash logs (`apanic_console`, `dmesg-ramoops`). No `-now-` names. About 54 bad paths per 10 minutes from bad log-directory settings. | The file-name rules must cover these or reject them on purpose (ADR 0007). |
| Phone models | VVX 75%, Edge E 25%, Trio 0.4%, CCX 0.3%. Nearly all uploads come from the Application stage, not the Updater. | Lab tests cover VVX and Edge E first. |
| TLS versions | Not measurable: the request log that records the TLS version is not sent to OCI. | Confirmed in the lab instead (TLS 1.2 only). |

1	# Lab results with real phones, 2026-10-16
2	
3	Phones: VVX 250 (firmware 6.4.6), Edge E220 (8.2.3), and a VVX 301 (5.9.x) for the TLS check only. No CCX was
4	available. Uploaded bodies were deleted after the session because they held real call history. Each row names the
5	decision it settled.
6	
7	| Check | Result | What it changed |
8	|---|---|---|
9	| Content-Length | Always sent, never chunked. `Expect: 100-continue` on every PUT. No Content-Range. | Keep the 411 rule; the service and the ALB must handle 100-continue (ADR 0009). |
10	| MAC in the certificate | Subject CN, 12 hex digits, uppercase, no separators. No SAN. File names carry the MAC in lowercase. | Read the MAC from the CN and compare case-insensitively (ADR 0004). |
11	| TLS | TLS 1.2 only on all three phones. Shared ciphers: ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 and ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384. | The ALB policy must allow these on TLS 1.2 (ADR 0003). |
12	| Certificate chain | Phones send 3 certificates (leaf and 2 intermediates); with the root the chain is 4. Device certificates are valid for 15 years. | Exactly at the ALB depth limit of 4, so it must be tested on a real ALB. Phones made before about late 2011 may carry expired certificates; how the ALB treats them is open. |
13	| Reaction to status codes | Retry only on 503: 3 tries, 1 s apart, identical body. Retry-After ignored. 405, 429, 413, 411, 400 and 403 get one try. A 503 sent after 100 Continue leaves app.log stuck for 300 s and holds back the phone's other uploads. | Always reject before 100 Continue. Never 503; prefer 429 when overloaded (ADR 0009). Keys must cope with identical calls.xml copies within 2 s (ADR 0011). |
14	| File names | `<mac>-app.log`, `<mac>-boot.log` (VVX only), `<mac>-calls.xml`. Manual upload: `<mac>-now-app.log`, `<mac>-now-boot.log`; `-now-` comes right after the MAC. | Accept `-now-` after the MAC. Don't require boot.log; the Edge never sends it (ADR 0007). |
15	| What each upload holds | app.log holds only the lines added since the last successful upload, plus any failed lines. `-now-` files and calls.xml are full copies every time. | Store the pieces; joining them in order rebuilds the log. Expect one full app.log per phone at migration. Nothing is lost on a 429. |
16	| Backlog after an outage | After a 15-minute outage the phone sends nothing until something new happens. No log lines or call-list changes were lost. A 1-5-9 call made during the outage was dropped. | No upload flood when the service comes back. |
17	| Other models | The Edge E220 behaves like the VVX 250 except it never sends boot.log and offers only 6 GCM ciphers. The VVX 301 matches the VVX 250 on TLS. | One design fits all three. |
18	| Sizes | app.log 283 B to 28.6 KB; calls.xml 18.5 to 64.8 KB. Every upload took under 35 ms on the LAN. No core dumps seen. | Small bodies. Core-dump sizes come from production data only (`2026-10-15-oci-measurements.md`). |
19	
20	Still open from the lab: whether the ALB accepts the phone's chain at depth 4, whether it overwrites client-sent
21	`X-Amzn-Mtls-*` headers (ADR 0004 is safe either way), and how it treats expired device certificates. These need a
22	real ALB, not the Envoy stand-in in `local/`.
23

  `api/openapi.yaml`. `OpenApiDocumentTest` reads the current path.
- How `build_for_gds.yaml` builds a second image and chart (the processor) from one repo. Noted in the processor
  Dockerfile.
- Production retention for index rows, which waits on the calls.xml privacy review (ADR 0008, ADR 0023).
- The herd-device-api endpoint for MAC to customer (ADR 0019).
- Whether the processor should also get a Helm chart in this repo, and its scaling in production (KEDA runs on stage-08
  only).

## Decided in the design doc, no record needed

Repo setup facts that are settings on GitHub rather than rules for code: repo name, default branch `develop`, production
branch `master`, one ruleset for both, the build8 job as the required check, squash into develop and merge commit into
master, build8 tags as the only release versions, no CODEOWNERS while two people work here. ADR 0016 lists them.

3	/**
4	 * Why an upload is refused: one reason per check in {@link UploadPolicy}, then what can go wrong once the body is read,
5	 * in {@code upload.UploadFlow}. Each reason has its status code in {@code web.RejectionStatusMapper} and its response
6	 * in openapi.yaml, so adding one means updating both, and the parameterized web test.
7	 */
8	public enum Rejection {
9	
10	    /** The path after /logs/ is not an accepted file name. 400. */
11	    BAD_FILE_NAME,
12	
13	    /** The file type is turned off in device-logs.file-types, as calls.xml is by default. 403. */
14	    FILE_TYPE_DISABLED,
15	
16	    /** The ALB headers do not establish who is calling. 403. */
17	    UNTRUSTED_IDENTITY,
18	
19	    /** The certificate MAC differs from the MAC in the file name. 403. */
20	    MAC_MISMATCH,
21	
22	    /** The request has no Content-Length, for example because it is chunked. 411. */
23	    LENGTH_REQUIRED,
24	
25	    /** Content-Length is above the type's max-size. 413. */
26	    TOO_LARGE,
27	
28	    /**
29	     * The connection ended before Content-Length bytes arrived. Tomcat answers 400 itself when its read of the body
30	     * fails, so this records the same code.
31	     */
32	    BODY_INCOMPLETE,
33	
34	    /** The body stopped arriving for longer than Tomcat's connection timeout. Tomcat answers 408 itself, as above. */
35	    BODY_TIMEOUT,
36	
37	    /** An object already has this key, so the create-only write was refused and nothing was overwritten. 429. */
38	    KEY_EXISTS,
39	
40	    /** The write to storage failed or ran past its deadline. The file may still have been stored. 429, never 503. */
41	    STORAGE_FAILED
42	}

content.text:
**Is it safe?** Yes, according to the one measurement in the repo. A full day of production pccfg logs (2026-10-15, us-phoenix-1) showed PUTs per MAC per 10 minutes at median 1, p99 6 and max 114. Only one MAC went over 30. The research note says 30 per 10 minutes "is safe for normal phones and catches the outlier." That is only one weekday in one region, and OCI keeps logs for 5 to 7 days, so it can't be measured again.

**What status does an over-limit phone get?** 429, under ADR 0009. The lab found that phones don't retry a 429 and lose nothing, because app.log carries its lines into the next upload. However, the limit isn't enforced yet:
- `InMemoryRateLimiter` exists but nothing calls it ("not wired yet").
- `Rejection.java` has no rate-limit reason.
- `openapi.yaml` still says "Still to add: 429 for the rate limit."
- The `device-logs.rate-limit.per-mac.*` settings are listed under "Designed, not in the code yet" and aren't in `DeviceLogsProperties`.

**Can it move to a shared counter?** The design allows for it, but not without a new decision. ADR 0010 counts uploads per pod in memory behind a `RateLimiter` interface, so a shared version can replace it without changing callers. Its rule, though, says no network call (Redis, Valkey) on the upload path without a new record. Moving it means writing an ADR that supersedes 0010 and asking a person first.
